text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said he did not expect parliament to approve any significant changes to the proposed 1997 state budget, planned with a deficit of around 37 billion crowns.
- President Michal Kovac and Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik on Sunday left for an Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) summit, starting today in Lisbon.

- Defence Minister Jan Sitek said Slovakia was interested in purchasing Russian KAMO-52 helicopters and JAK-30 aeroplanes. The equipment should be delivered in part repayment of Russian debts to Slovakia, Sitek said.

- Ivan Saktor, President of the Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ), said KOZ would not sign next year's general agreement with the government if parliament ignors all its proposed amendments to the 1997 state budget. Saktor said the proposed budget, if approved, could result in social conflict.
- The troubled heavy engineering company and major arms producer Povazske Strojarne a.s., claims it is owed some 1.3 billion crowns.

PRAVDA - The 1997 draft budget includes a paragraph according to which any claim against the Slovak Republic which had not been acknowledged by the government can not be registered as government debt to the central bank. This may finally end arguments with the Czech Republic over some 24 billion crowns in debts, claimed by the Czechs but never acknowledged by the Slovak side.
- Dozens of Slovak trucks were cought in the 12-day nation-wide truckers strike in France. Financial damages from the strike, promised by the French government, will be calculated next week.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The National Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, plans to sell property worth some 70 billion crowns next year. The NPF said it expected 1997 revenues of 15.8 billion crowns, of which 4.7 billion should come in cash and 11.1 billion crowns should be paid in privatisation bonds.
- Slovakia has signed a free-trade agreement with Lithuania effective January 1.
- Alcatel SEL TLH has signed a contract with the state telecom monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie, worth some 1.08 billion crowns, for supplies of digital exchanges next year.
